repo_notes.content: Published to npm as @dcyfr/ai under MIT. The framework lives entirely under packages/ai/.
repo_notes.author: rei-doc-specialist

repo_notes.content: The largest subsystems by file count are manifests/ (85), src/plugins/ (47) and delegation/ (50 plus 20 tests). Document those before the smaller ones.
repo_notes.author: rei-doc-specialist

repo_notes.content: There is no packages/ai/llm/ directory. Provider code, where it exists, sits under src/integrations/ and src/gateway/.
repo_notes.author: rei-doc-specialist

pages.title: Framework Architecture
pages.purpose: How @dcyfr/ai is put together: the package layout under packages/ai/, the agent lifecycle end to end, and which subsystem owns which decision.

pages.title: Agent Manifests
pages.purpose: The manifest format that defines an agent: YAML front matter plus a markdown body, the capability vocabulary under manifests/capabilities/, validation, and how a manifest is loaded.

pages.title: Built-in Agents
pages.purpose: The agents shipped with the framework under agents-builtin/, grouped by the domain each covers, and what a caller gets from each.

pages.title: Delegation
pages.purpose: How one agent hands work to another: the delegation middleware chain, routing rules, budget and depth limits, and failure handling.

pages.title: Plugin System
pages.purpose: The plugin surface under src/plugins/ and plugins/pilot/: manifest shape, lifecycle hooks, the sandbox boundary, and how a third-party plugin is loaded and constrained.

pages.title: MCP Servers
pages.purpose: The Model Context Protocol servers under mcp/servers/: what each exposes, how tools are registered, and how a server is discovered at runtime.

pages.title: Memory and Compaction
pages.purpose: Agent memory: what is retained between turns, the compaction strategy that keeps a conversation inside its budget, and the session boundary.

pages.title: Metacognition and Verification
pages.purpose: The self-assessment layer: metacognition checks, the reputation signal, output verification, and the circuit breaker that stops an unproductive loop.

pages.title: Runtime and Execution
pages.purpose: Executing an agent: the container abstraction, the scheduler, resource limits, telemetry, and the permission checks applied on the way in.

pages.title: Development Guide
pages.purpose: Writing a custom agent, a plugin or an MCP server against this framework, plus the test and doc-parity tooling used in this repo.

pages.title: API Reference
pages.purpose: The exported TypeScript surface: core types, manifest schema, delegation and plugin interfaces, and the MCP protocol types.
